thread:
anya: Heads up — after rolling the new kernel routing in v3.7.1 we're seeing a measurable drop in lead-token (tokens 1-5) cache hit rate across several ded. pools (~15-25%). Reverting the routing selection on one pool restored hit rate. Anyone else seeing this?

deploy-bot: Deployed runtime v3.7.1 -> prod/eng-runtime at 2026-03-17T16:02Z :rocket:

kevin: seeing the same on rdlb-alpha and rdlb-beta. Lead-token hits down, tail looks fine. Also noticed batcher.avg_fanout jumped which increased p99 a bit.

sasha: grabbed traces from node g4-07 in dedicated-west. Short snippet below — looks like a key normalization mismatch count spiked after routing switched to hybrid kernel selection.

```
kernel_variant: fused_attn_v2 -> hybrid_routing_v1
kv_cache.leading_token.hit_rate_percent: 78 -> 61
kv_cache.total.lookups: 12034
prefix_key_norm.mismatch_count: 412
routing.hash.seed: 0x1a2b3c -> 0x4f5e6d
batcher.avg_fanout: 1.8 -> 2.6
```

sasha: My read — the hybrid routing path changed how we serialize/pad the prefill segment before hashing (padding order moved ahead of a small canonicalization step). That makes identical logical prefixes get hashed differently, so warmstarts miss.

leo: I repro locally with runtime:v3.7.1 + model q8_0 quant flags. The routing.hash.seed changed and padding ordering shift is enough to flip the prefix hash. If quantization path toggles canonical tokenization for certain attention kernels, we get different byte sequences.

kevin: can we gate kernel selection behind a compatibility flag that preserves prior padding/seed behavior? Short-term we should revert routing on stable pools. Longer-term we need a canonical normalizer independent of kernel internals.

anya: rolling back routing selection to previous behavior for affected dedicated pools now. @perf-bot can you run a 1h KV hit-rate sweep across dedicated-west and report per-token hit curve (t=1..10)?

perf-bot: Scheduled job perf/kv-hitrate-sweep for cluster dedicated-west. ETA ~30m, will post charts to #eng-runtime when done.

leo: i'll open a minimal repro and add a unit test asserting normalized prefix bytes are identical across kernel variants. Also adding an integration eval that checks priming hit at tokens 1-5 for a handful of prompt families.

kevin: good. also add a migration plan: when we change canonicalization again we should emit a compatibility salt and a rolling backfill to avoid long misswaves.

anya: +1. holding rollback for now until perf-bot confirms stable hit recovery. After that we should schedule an RFC for explicit key-normalization, add telemetry for "prefix_normalizer_version" and include it in rollout gates.

sasha: opening the RFC and a short postmortem draft now — will include repro steps (docker runtime:v3.7.1 + q8_0), traces, and a suggested patch to the routing selector to keep canonicalization consistent.

kevin: thanks — ping me when the rollback completes and attach the perf charts. :thumbsup:
